subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & EU/APAC quality checks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@globexretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & EU/APAC quality checks

Hi Claire (and team),

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard:
- High priority: customer-facing search + FAQ assistant in EU locales (FR, DE, ES, IT, NL) and select APAC locales (JA, KO, ZH-TW).
- Success criteria: localization quality on par with current English baseline (no more than 10% regression on key intents), latency target <300ms p95, and predictable per-token cost.

Initial model fit recommendations:
- Baseline for eval: redwood-medium-7b-q4 (good latency/cost balance)
- High-quality option: redwood-13b-llama-q4 or rw-13b-pt-quant (better multilingual QA)
- Low-cost fallback: redwood-latest-3b-quant (for scale testing)

What we'll deliver next:
1) Shared prompt set + recommended eval harness (CSV + eval script) — attaching multilingual_prompt_sets_v2.csv and a benchmark summary PDF.
2) Run initial automated eval across priority locales and return per-locale metrics (BLEU / chrF / intent accuracy) within ~7 business days after we receive your sample prompts/annotations.
3) Human spot checks and calibration plan for any locale with >8% regression.

Requests from you:
- Priority locales list (confirm the EU/APAC items above or reorder).
- Sample prompts or typical user messages (10-20 per locale) and any locale-specific formatting constraints.
- Success criteria and any regulatory constraints (data residency / redaction) for each region.

Links: Redwood eval harness (drive) - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example
HubSpot: hs-GLX-4209

I'll follow up after Marissa and Neha review the prompt sets we attached.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Claire Park <claire.park@globexretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-07T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & EU/APAC quality checks

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- GDPR/data residency: for EU production we need to keep logs for 90 days and cannot persist raw user PII. Our legal team will want a short note on how Redwood handles redaction/audit logs.
- For the APAC locales, Japanese and Korean are higher priority than Traditional Chinese for the first phase.

I've attached a small set of sample prompts we use for the customer FAQ assistant (will upload to the shared drive). Can Redwood run the initial eval on our behalf, or do you expect us to run locally?

Claire Park
Head of Product, Globex Retail
claire.park@globexretail.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@globexretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-07T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & EU/APAC quality checks

Hi Claire - great, thanks for the sample prompts. We can run the initial automated eval on your behalf (recommended) and share both the raw metrics and the evaluation harness if you prefer to run in parallel. 

Proposed eval plan (high level):
- Automated pass: run the prompt set through three model candidates (redwood-medium-7b-q4, redwood-13b-llama-q4, redwood-latest-3b-quant) across the priority locales. We'll report BLEU, chrF, intent accuracy, and latency p50/p95.
- Human calibration: stratified sampling per-locale for human rating where automated metrics are ambiguous - we'll flag locales >8% regression for manual review.

Attachments included: multilingual_prompt_sets_v2.csv, redwood_benchmarks_eu_apac.pdf (summary).

Next steps:
- Can you confirm final locale priority (your latest note: JA, KO first for APAC; FR, DE, ES, IT, NL for EU) and confirm if we should exclude any PII fields from the uploads?
- I'll kick off the eval as soon as we have the final list and your confirmation that Redwood can run the tests on your sample prompts. Expected first-pass results in ~5 business days.

Thanks - looping in Marissa for any technical follow-ups.

Best,
Vanessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Claire Park <claire.park@globexretail.com>
Date: 2027-07-08T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Multilingual model fit & EU/APAC quality checks

Adding a few technical notes from the solutions side: 

- Quality regression plan: when we run the automated pass we'll compute delta vs English baseline for intent accuracy and chrF. If a locale shows >8% delta we run a human spot-check (n=100) to identify common failure modes (hallucination, mistranslation, tokenization issues).
- Locale-specific prompts: for languages with complex tokenization (JA, KO, ZH) we recommend including tokenized variants in the prompt set and adding a short system instruction that enforces brevity for UI rendering.
- Benchmarks: the attached PDF has previous Redwood runs on retail conversational queries in EU languages - useful as a baseline.
- Timeline: assuming we can run on your sample prompts, expect automated metrics in 5 business days and the human calibration pass in an additional 3-5 business days depending on scope.

I'll also add a small eval checklist (locale-specific tokenization, punctuation normalization, date/number formats) to the shared drive.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
